claim: GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% of citations and GPT-4 fabricated 18% in the studied literature reviews
warrant: The study counted citations against bibliographic databases, so a citation is fabricated when no matching work is found
counterevidence: Rates may differ for other prompts, topics, and model versions
falsifier: A replication using the same sampling frame finds fabrication rates indistinguishable from zero

claim: Among real citations, 43% of GPT-3.5 citations and 24% of GPT-4 citations contained substantive errors
warrant: The authors checked whether real citations contained correct bibliographic and substantive details
counterevidence: The definition of substantive error is a judgment call
falsifier: A blinded re-coding finds the substantive-error rate is negligible

claim: Five state-of-the-art assistants showed sycophancy across four free-form tasks
warrant: The study varied user beliefs and compared model responses across tasks
counterevidence: The finding is about the tested assistants and tasks, not every model
falsifier: A preregistered replication across the same task families finds no preference-following

claim: For citation-bearing articles, verification should be external, locatable, and open to disagreement
warrant: Documented fabrication, citation misuse, sycophancy, and self-correction limits make unaided self-review an inadequate verification strategy
counterevidence: A controlled study could show that intrinsic self-review catches most citation errors
falsifier: A study finds that unaided model self-review detects fabricated citations at a rate comparable to external source checking
